title: Tests: send FileIdTest's media once, and retry failed Bot API connections
body:
The v8 run after #1934 (40705728442) failed in `test`: FileIdTest's data provider got `false` from `file_get_contents` for the Bot API's `sendsticker`. The log has `SSL: Connection reset by peer` / `Failed to enable crypto`: api.telegram.org reset the TLS handshake. That became a `json_decode(false)` TypeError, which made the provider invalid.

- **Sent once:** the provider is a generator, so PHPUnit ran it once for `testDownload` and again for `testResendConvert`, sending every file to the Bot API twice. It now runs once and its result is cached.
- **Retries and errors:** every Bot API call goes through a curl helper. It retries a failed connection twice, with a backoff, and throws with the Bot API's description when the call fails (`{"ok":false,...}`) instead of passing `false` on.

Not changed: the Bot API still fetches the test files by URL, and `https://daniil.it/audio_2020-02-01_18-09-08.ogg` (the voice) returns 404 now. It still passed on this run, maybe because Telegram caches the URL.

title: Tests: don't download the media sent by URL on every run
body:
The v8 build after #1933 failed (run 40702637041, job `build`): `tests/testing.php` fetched `tests/faust.jpg` and `tests/60` from `github.com/danog/MadelineProto/raw/v8` through `fileGetContents` to have something to compare Telegram's copies with. The response took longer than amphp's default 10 s transfer timeout (the same job also failed to connect to phar.madelineproto.xyz, so GitHub was slow then).

Those URLs point to the files of this directory, so the test now reads them locally, and only Telegram fetches the URLs. This is the "tests download nothing per run" rule.

title: Read MP4 composition offsets as signed in every box version
body:
Playing https://t.me/danog_community/368574 (H.264 with B-frames, AAC) with `/play` wedged magnaluna's video in the group call, even after `/skip`.

**Mechanism**: the file's `ctts` box is version 0 but holds negative composition offsets (Telegram's clients write them this way, and ffmpeg reads them as signed in every version). `Mp4` read version 0 offsets as unsigned, so every B-frame got a timestamp of ~2³² ticks (47721892 ms, ~13 hours). Then:
- `VideoPlaybackTrack` held the first such frame as pending and slept in `delay()` until it was due, 13 hours later. A skip can't wake that wait, so the call's video stayed stuck through `/skip` and the default video that followed (only the audio went on).
- `bufferedUntilMs` jumped by 13 hours too, so the reader's throttle stopped reading.

**Fix**: read `ctts` and `trun` composition offsets as signed whatever the box version. Matroska's relative block timecodes were already signed.

Regression test: `Mp4Test` now also demuxes an MP4 with negative offsets whose `ctts` version was rewritten to 0. It fails without the fix, and the user's file now demuxes to ffprobe's timestamps (0–7533 ms, 227 frames).

title: Changelog: send it to @madelineprotophar, and to -1001375152824
body:
`tests/announce_release.php` sends each release's changelog:

- to **@madelineprotophar** instead of @MadelineProto (not pinned, as before);
- also to **-1001375152824**, where the first message is pinned, as in @pwrtelegramgroupru.

`DRY_RUN=1 tests/announce_release.php 8.14.0` lists the four chats and the two pins:

```
--- message 1/1 to @madelineprotophar: 1249 characters, 24 entities of size 1690
--- message 1/1 to @MadeLine_Farsi: 1249 characters, 24 entities of size 1690
--- message 1/1 to @pwrtelegramgroupru: 1249 characters, 24 entities of size 1690
--- pin message 1 in @pwrtelegramgroupru
--- message 1/1 to -1001375152824: 1249 characters, 24 entities of size 1690
--- pin message 1 in -1001375152824
```

The bot of `PHAR_BOT_TOKEN` must be a member of -1001375152824 with the right to pin messages (not checked here: the token is only in CI).

Internal: `tests/` doesn't ship.
